The ReadLog code doesn't handle a line which is longer than 65k bytes gracefully.

Ideally, the "token too long" error should be ignored and continue reading the logs.

> The ReadLog code doesn't handle a line which is longer than 65k bytes gracefully. No, it doesn't need to. The line will be truncated if it is too long before writing. https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/4011821c946e8db032be86266dd9364ccb204118/modules/actions/log.go#L144-L149 I think the real reason is that the log file is broken. It may be related to the malfunction of NFS on gitea.com a few days ago. I logged on to the machine and downloaded the original log files: --- And all is well after re-run.
I agree that errors should be visible in the UI. But I have no idea how to do that, so I will remove self-assignee.
How many "nil" chars there? Could there be a bug in DBFS code?

> How many "nil" chars there? Could there be a bug in DBFS code?

The number of "nil" chars doesn't really matter. Since the total file size matches the file size recorded in the DB, and the "nil" chars end at the beginning of a line, it couldn't be that the DBFS lost some blocks.

It seems like it opened a non-existent file in DBFS , seek and write, but I have no idea how it could have happened. I will continue to track this bug to see if it happens again.

I confirmed that it is a bug and figured out the way to reproduce it. It's not related to DBFS or FS malfunction, but the logic of writing action logs.

I'll fix it.

issue.body:
Fix #25451.

Bugfixes:
- When stopping the zombie or endless tasks, set `LogInStorage` to true after transferring the file to storage. It was missing, it could write to a nonexistent file in DBFS because `LogInStorage` was false.
- Always update `ActionTask.Updated` when there's a new state reported by the runner, even if there's no change. This is to avoid the task being judged as a zombie task.

Enhancement:
- Support `Stat()` for DBFS file.
- `WriteLogs` refuses to write if it could result in content holes.
